events.message: Core code panicked at the {boundary} boundary

boundary.description: Where the panic ends: request when the dispatcher turned it into a failed response and Core kept running, thread when it unwinds a Core thread whose owner decides what happens next

panic.description: Panic message from the Rust payload, or a fixed note when the payload is not text
panic.reason: A Rust panic message is free text written at the panic site, often with the Debug output of an error, and has no stable code; keep its wording after Core redaction and the 1 KiB cap

location.description: Source file, line and column the compiler attached to the panic
location.reason: The compiler reports the panic site as a source path with line and column; dependency paths can be absolute, so Core redacts the text and caps it at 1 KiB instead of treating it as a stable identifier

method.description: Core protocol method the request was running when boundary is request, e.g. git.write

boundary.description: Recover site: viva: followed by the UI framework boundary such as viva:darwin:appkit-callback, or core:events-observer and core:log-waker for Core callbacks

panic.description: Panic value as text, as the recovering boundary received it
panic.reason: A recovered Go panic value is arbitrary text with no stable code; keep its wording so the failing check can be found, after Core redaction and the 1 KiB cap

stack.description: Frames of the panicking goroutine from the panic call outward, joined on one line
stack.reason: A Go stack trace has no structured equivalent; the host keeps only the frames after the panic call as function file:line pairs with base file names, and Core redacts and caps the text at 1 KiB

events.message: Window loop stopped with an error

error.description: Error the UI framework returned when its window loop ended for a reason other than a recovered panic

events.message: Previous session ended in a crash

session.description: Log directory of the session that crashed, so its last records can be read next to this one

panic.description: First line the Go runtime printed when the process died, such as panic: or fatal error:
panic.reason: The Go runtime prints the cause of a fatal crash only as text in its crash output; keep the first line after Core redaction and the 1 KiB cap

stack.description: Frames of the goroutine that crashed, from its panic call outward, joined on one line
stack.reason: A Go stack trace has no structured equivalent; the host keeps only the frames after the panic call as function file:line pairs with base file names, and Core redacts and caps the text at 1 KiB

events.message: Previous session ended without closing its log

session.description: Log directory of the session that was killed, force quit or stopped by a native crash before closing its log

stage.description: Step that failed: create when this session's crash file could not be made, so a fatal crash of this session is not recorded; claim when a previous session's crash file could not be read or removed; release when Close could not remove this session's file, so the next start reports this session as not closed

error.description: Filesystem or runtime error of that step
